scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

*   **Creative outlet:** For many, makeup is a creative outlet. It allows for expression and experimentation, which can be very satisfying.
*   **Personal ritual:** Having a consistent morning ritual, especially one you enjoy, can provide a sense of stability and control in your daily life.

Ultimately, if it makes you feel good, confident, and ready to face the day, then it's absolutely the right thing for *you* to do. Don't let anyone tell you that taking time for yourself in this way isn't valuable. Keep enjoying your makeup routine!
